subject: Inference deployment pathway — dedicated sizing recap & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Murphy <ellie@cinchhealth.ai>, Tom Park <tom.park@cinchhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-12T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Quick recap + follow-ups from today's call

Hi Ellie / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the items we left with as next steps so we can size Dedicated appropriately. TL;DR: you indicated a preference for a dedicated/reserved environment (VPC-first) but want options for on-prem later — we sketched three deployment pathways and need a small traffic sample to validate throughput.

Key context from call:
- Primary workload: user-facing conversational search (short prompts) + a smaller batch job for long-document summarization.
- Peak observed activity window: 11am–2pm PT, expected burst TPS ~150–200 for short prompts; sustained background summarization ~10–25 TPS.
- Typical token mix: short queries ~15–40 tokens output (1–4 prompts per second), summarization jobs produce ~2k–5k tokens per job.
- Latency target: p95 generation under 350ms for short queries; summarization can be >2s.
- Data controls: must run in customer VPC with private peering; eventual desire to support on-prem air-gapped for regulated clients (Phase 2).

What we need from you to progress the Dedicated sizing + quote:
1) Small traffic sample (CSV) showing timestamps + request type (short vs long) for a 24–72h window — helps us model real concurrency.
2) A representative token profile (input/output mean & p50/p95) if you have it — otherwise we can infer from the sample.
3) Any hard constraints on GPU vendor preference (NVIDIA H100 vs A100) or procurement restrictions.

Our proposed next steps after we get those two artifacts:
- Marissa (solutions eng) will run a quick throughput simulation and propose two sizing options: cost-optimized (A100-heavy) and latency/SLO-optimized (H100-heavy) with fallbacks and padding for burst.
- I will prepare a short mutual action plan and a draft reserved-capacity quote for your procurement team.

Attachments: none yet — please attach the CSV + token profile in reply.

Thanks —

Jordan —

Thanks, appreciate the recap. Attached are the two files you asked for: cinch_traffic_sample.csv and cinch_token_profile.json. Quick notes to make sure the team interprets them correctly:

- Peak burst: we've seen spikes up to ~180 TPS for short queries (mostly token-completion prompts used in chat widgets). Sustained short-query load is ~70–90 TPS outside peak windows.
- Summarization: batch jobs are queued and run asynchronously; when they run concurrently we see ~12–20 TPS (each job produces ~2k–4k tokens).
- Token profile: short queries average 28 output tokens and ~12 input tokens; summarization jobs average ~3.1k output tokens.
- Preferred path: we want Dedicated in a VPC with private peering for now. On-prem is a Phase 2 ask (timeline TBD).
- GPUs: procurement is neutral but finance prefers keeping options open; no strict vendor lock.

Attached: cinch_traffic_sample.csv (CSV, 48k rows — excerpt attached), cinch_token_profile.json (JSON).

> Thanks, appreciate the recap. Attached are the two files you asked for...

Ellie / Tom —

I pulled the sample and ran a quick simulation to translate the traffic into candidate Dedicated pools. Below are two concrete pathways. These are conservative — we'll finalize after an internal perf run with the exact token distributions.

Scenario A — Latency/SLO optimized (H100-forward):
- Peak target modeled: 200 TPS short (p95 target <350ms), 20 TPS summarization concurrently.
- Model assumptions: using an Llama2-Chat-class 70B FP16 or quantized variant; average short-query token round-trip ~40 tokens.
- Recommended baseline: 4 x H100-80GB (reserved), with autoscale buffer to add 1 additional H100 on sustained growth.
- Expected behavior: p95 latency headroom for short queries, low queuing during bursts, good memory envelope for large KV caches for chat state.
- Notes: higher upfront cost, best p95/95 latency.

Scenario B — Cost-optimized (A100-80GB heavier):
- Peak target: same modeled 200 TPS short / 20 TPS summarize.
- Recommended baseline: 6 x A100-80GB (reserved) with careful batching and aggressive KV cache tuning.
- Expected behavior: slightly higher p95, but lower hourly cost — good trade-off if you can tolerate occasional 400–600ms tail.

Sizing rationale & concurrency math (brief):
- Measured tokens/sec per GPU (approx): H100 ~16k tokens/sec (short-query mix), A100 ~10–12k tokens/sec depending on quantization and model variant.
- Peak total token/sec target (observed): short queries ~200 TPS * 40 tokens = ~8k tokens/sec; summarization (20 TPS * 3000 avg tokens) = ~60k tokens/sec but these are batch jobs distributed over longer windows — we handle via batching and off-peak scheduling where possible.
- Because summarization is bursty and costly in tokens, we recommend isolating summarization onto a separate pool or using lower-priority repurposing nodes to avoid interference with low-latency short queries.

Operational notes / next steps:
1) Jordan: I'll produce a short tech appendix that shows expected p95/P50 for each pathway and a fallback policy (e.g., route to smaller model variant under pressure).
2) Jordan will send a reserved-capacity quote (monthly commit) and a slide outlining the Mutual Action Plan.
3) Ellie: if you can confirm any procurement constraints (term length, PO process), we'll include that in the quote.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_quote_v1.pdf (draft estimate), link to internal sizing notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/compact/token-metrics

-Marissa
